## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kappamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Kappa") is a verse discourse located in the *Pārāyaṇavagga*, the fifth chapter of the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 5.11, PTS Snp 211), beginning around verse 1092 [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1994; Norman 1997–2001]. In this sutta, the student Kappa addresses the Buddha to ask about the island that provides refuge amidst the overwhelming flood and the perils of birth [SuttaCentral]. Secondary treatments frequently list the work as one of the successive question-dialogues (*pucchā*) of the *Pārāyaṇavagga* [Hazra 1994; Saddhatissa 2013].

In terms of commentary and canonical cross-references, the sutta is preserved and commented upon in the *Cullaniddesa*, specifically in the *Kappamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 14) and the *Pucchā* (Cnd 2) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus aligns 26 matching passages across these two texts: 23 matches (1,435 characters) with Cnd 14 (with the longest shared sequence at segments §0.2–2.5 matching Cnd 14 §12.4–14.5) and 3 matches (995 characters) with Cnd 2 (segments §0.2–0.1 matching Cnd 2 §61.0–65.0) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections meet the match threshold in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].

The sutta is widely translated, with SuttaCentral recording 15 translations across 12 modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
